title: Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana Rajasthan: Free Phone Guide
meta_description: Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana gives free smartphones to eligible women in Rajasthan. Rs 6,800 e-wallet, 3-yr data. Visit igsy.rajasthan.gov.in.

hero.one_liner: Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana gave free smartphones to about 40 lakh Rajasthan women in Phase 1. Phase 2 has stalled under the new government. Check your status.

what_is_it: Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana is a Rajasthan government scheme that provides free smartphones with a SIM card and three years of free internet to eligible women and girl students across the state. The scheme transfers Rs 6,800 into the beneficiary's e-wallet, of which Rs 6,175 covers the cost of the smartphone and Rs 625 covers the SIM card and data plan.

The first phase of the scheme covered 40 lakh women and girl students who received smartphones at designated Indira Gandhi Smartphone Scheme camps across the state. The remaining approximately 95 lakh beneficiaries are being covered in the second phase of distribution.

how_to_apply.title: Check your eligibility on the Jan Soochna Portal
how_to_apply.description: Visit jansoochna.rajasthan.gov.in and look for the Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana section. Enter your Jan Aadhaar number to check whether your name appears in the beneficiary list for the scheme.

how_to_apply.title: Confirm your family's Chiranjeevi registration
how_to_apply.description: The scheme is primarily for women in Chiranjeevi-registered families. Confirm that your family is registered under the Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana, as this is the base database used for identifying eligible households.

how_to_apply.title: Find the nearest camp date and location
how_to_apply.description: Distribution happens through dedicated IGSY camps in each district. Check the camp schedule for your area by visiting igsy.rajasthan.gov.in, calling helpline 181, or checking your local gram panchayat or ward office notice board.

how_to_apply.title: Gather required documents before the camp
how_to_apply.description: Carry your Jan Aadhaar card, your Aadhaar card, and a passport-size photograph to the distribution camp. The Jan Aadhaar number is used to verify your name in the beneficiary database at the camp.

how_to_apply.title: Attend the camp to receive your smartphone
how_to_apply.description: At the distribution camp, officials will verify your documents and confirm your eligibility. Once verified, the Rs 6,800 amount will be credited to your e-wallet and you will receive the smartphone and SIM card at the camp itself.

how_to_apply.title: Activate the SIM and set up your phone
how_to_apply.description: The SIM card included with the smartphone comes with three years of free internet data. Activate the SIM at the camp or immediately after, following the instructions given by the camp volunteers or the telecom partner.

ministry: Department of Information Technology and Communication (DoIT&C), Rajasthan

extra_sections.heading: What Is Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana
content: This scheme specifically targets women and girls from Chiranjeevi-registered families and other vulnerable categories including widow and destitute pension recipients. The primary goal is to close the digital access gap for women in Rajasthan by giving them direct ownership of a smartphone and internet connectivity.

The four 'Indira Gandhi' schemes in Rajasthan are completely separate programmes and should not be confused with each other. This page covers only the Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana (free smartphones); other schemes under the Indira Gandhi name cover topics like old-age pension, women's monthly cash support, and urban employment and belong to separate pages.

Women who are eligible for this scheme but have not yet received their smartphone should check their eligibility status on the Jan Soochna Portal at jansoochna.rajasthan.gov.in or call the helpline at 181 to find out the current camp schedule in their area.

The scheme does not require women to purchase the smartphone themselves at any point. The amount is credited to the e-wallet linked to the beneficiary's Jan Aadhaar number, and the smartphone is provided at the camp distribution event.

The Jan Soochna Portal at jansoochna.rajasthan.gov.in also provides information about this scheme including eligibility check by Jan Aadhaar number, beneficiary list lookup, and links to camp-related announcements.

extra_sections.title: Current Status: Phase 2 Is Stalled
extra_sections.content:
This was a flagship scheme of the previous Congress government, launched in August 2023 just before the December 2023 election. Phase 1 distributed about 40 lakh smartphones.

After the change of government, Phase 2 stalled. Of roughly 1.33 crore targeted women, only about 24.5 lakh had received phones, and the matter has been under review and questioned in the High Court. Treat distribution as paused, and check the portal for any official restart.

extra_sections.heading: Who Was Eligible
content: Rajasthan's Chiranjeevi Health Insurance Scheme is used as the base family database for identifying and verifying eligible households for this scheme. Families registered under Chiranjeevi and belonging to the eligible categories can verify whether their female members appear on the scheme's beneficiary list.

The official portal for this scheme is igsy.rajasthan.gov.in. The Jan Soochna Portal at jansoochna.rajasthan.gov.in also provides information about camp schedules and beneficiary lists for this scheme.

The scheme is important from a digital literacy standpoint as well. With a smartphone and three years of data, women can access government services, education portals, banking applications, and health information independently without relying on others.

The scheme was first announced by Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot in his 2023-24 budget speech as part of the state government's commitment to expanding digital access for women. It is one of the largest free smartphone distribution programmes run by any state government in India.

For any query, complaint, or information about the current distribution status in a specific area, the dedicated toll-free helpline is 181. This number is active during government working hours and is staffed to handle IGSY-related calls.

extra_sections.heading: The Eligibility Categories
content: Each smartphone distributed under this scheme is loaded with Rajasthan Sampark and other key government service apps as pre-installed software. This makes it easier for first-time users to immediately access government portals without searching for and installing apps separately.

The benefit under this scheme is entirely separate from any benefit under other Indira Gandhi schemes running in Rajasthan. A woman receiving pension under another Indira Gandhi scheme remains separately eligible for a smartphone under IGSY and should not be told otherwise at any camp.

Women who are first-time smartphone users can access digital literacy training through government programmes that run alongside IGSY in many districts. Camp organisers typically provide a brief orientation session on using the phone, accessing apps, and activating the SIM.

All beneficiaries under this scheme must come from families registered under the Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana, which is Rajasthan's state health insurance scheme. Women whose families are not registered under Chiranjeevi need to first get that registration done to become eligible.
Women who received a smartphone in Phase 1 are not eligible to receive another device in Phase 2. Each eligible woman receives one smartphone under the scheme.

extra_sections.heading: What the Benefit Included
content: Widow and destitute women who receive a Rajasthan state social security pension are directly eligible for a free smartphone under this scheme. The state pension database is linked to the IGSY beneficiary list.

Girl students enrolled in government schools from Class 9 to Class 12 are eligible for a smartphone. The enrollment must be in a government school and the girl must be studying in the eligible class during the year of the distribution camp.

Girls enrolled in government colleges, universities, polytechnic institutes, or Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) are also eligible. The college or institute must be a government-run institution for the girl to qualify under this category.

Women who have completed 100 days of work under MNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act) are eligible. This category ensures women from rural households who have worked under the employment guarantee scheme also get access to smartphones.

The three-year free internet included with the SIM is a significant part of the benefit. Women in rural and semi-urban areas of Rajasthan typically pay Rs 150-200 per month for data, meaning the SIM alone provides value of approximately Rs 5,000-7,000 over three years.

extra_sections.title: The E-wallet Credit
extra_sections.desc:
Rather than buying a phone, the beneficiary got Rs 6,800 credited to her Jan Aadhaar-linked account at the camp, used toward the smartphone and SIM.

The phone came with three years of free data, loaded with Rajasthan government service apps. It was a non-refundable grant.

extra_sections.heading: How Distribution Worked
content: Women who have completed 50 days of work under the Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Scheme (IGSRGS), which is the urban counterpart of MNREGA, are also eligible. This covers urban women who have worked under the state's urban employment programme.

The scheme is specifically for women, and male family members are not eligible even if the family is Chiranjeevi-registered. Each eligible woman in a qualifying household may receive her own smartphone separately.

A woman may fall under more than one eligible category at the same time. For example, a widow who is also an MNREGA worker or a college student who also belongs to a widow household both remain eligible under the relevant category.

Jan Aadhaar is the main identification tool for verifying eligibility. Every eligible woman must have a Jan Aadhaar card linked to her household, as the e-wallet credit and camp verification both work through the Jan Aadhaar system.

The scheme has been specifically structured to benefit women who are among the most digitally excluded in Rajasthan: widows, students in rural government schools, and MNREGA workers. These are groups that are unlikely to purchase a smartphone independently in the near term.

steps.title: Check the beneficiary list
steps.desc: Women checked their name on jansoochna.rajasthan.gov.in or igsy.rajasthan.gov.in using their Jan Aadhaar number.

steps.title: Attend the camp
steps.desc: Eligible women attended a designated camp with their original Jan Aadhaar and Aadhaar cards for verification.

steps.title: Verification and credit
steps.desc: After biometric verification, Rs 6,800 was credited to the Jan Aadhaar-linked account at the time of distribution.

steps.title: Receive phone and SIM
steps.desc: The woman received a standard Android phone and SIM. Activation could take up to 48 hours; problems were to be raised at the camp.

extra_sections.heading: Checking Your Status
content: Women who were eligible in Phase 1 but missed the camp or could not attend should check whether their names are included in Phase 2 beneficiary lists. The Jan Soochna Portal and helpline 181 are the best channels to check current camp schedules and beneficiary list status.

The scheme does not have a minimum age restriction beyond what is implied by the eligibility categories. A Class 9 student is typically 13-14 years old, which makes this one of the few government scheme benefits that can reach girls in their early teens.
Beneficiaries do not need to pay back the cost of the smartphone or the SIM card. The Rs 6,800 is a non-refundable government grant credited to the e-wallet specifically for this purpose.

After receiving the smartphone, the beneficiary is free to use it for any purpose including accessing government services, education apps, banking, and personal communication. There is no restriction on usage beyond the initial purpose of digital empowerment.

Women who miss the distribution camp for a valid reason such as illness or travel should contact the district e-Mitra kendra or the local WCD (Women and Child Development) officer to inquire about rebooking or alternate distribution arrangements.

extra_sections.title: How to Check Your Name and Status
extra_sections.content:
Check the beneficiary list on jansoochna.rajasthan.gov.in or igsy.rajasthan.gov.in with your Jan Aadhaar number. The helpline is 181.

If your name was listed in Phase 1 but you never got a phone, keep the record and watch the portal, since Phase 2 distribution has not been clearly restarted.

extra_sections.heading: The Four Indira Gandhi Schemes
content: Women who have complaints about camps, issues with verification, or problems with e-wallet credits should call the dedicated helpline at 181. The helpline is specifically equipped to handle IGSY-related queries and escalations.

The annual household income of the family does not affect eligibility for this scheme. Eligibility is determined solely by category membership, such as widow pension status, school enrollment, or MNREGA work completion, not by the family's income level.

Girls in private schools or private colleges are not eligible under this scheme even if they are from Chiranjeevi-registered families. The school or college enrollment must specifically be in a government-run institution to qualify under the student category.

Jan Aadhaar is Rajasthan's unique family identity document and is central to the IGSY verification process. Every family in Rajasthan is expected to have a Jan Aadhaar card, and women without one should get registered through the nearest e-Mitra kiosk before applying.

The smartphone distributed under this scheme is a standard Android smartphone from an approved vendor. Beneficiaries do not get to choose the brand or model; the device is procured by the government through a tender process.

items.title: Separate programmes
items.sub: Rajasthan ran four different Indira Gandhi schemes. This smartphone scheme is separate from the others.

extra_sections.heading: What to Watch For
content: The government maintains separate lists for different eligible categories. A woman who falls under two categories, such as a widow who is also a government college student, may appear in more than one list but will receive only one smartphone in total.

Women who migrated from another state but now hold a Rajasthan Jan Aadhaar card and are enrolled in an eligible category within Rajasthan are eligible for the scheme. Eligibility is based on current Rajasthan registration and category membership, not the state of birth.

Women who were listed in Phase 1 but did not attend the camp for any reason should check the Phase 2 beneficiary list separately. Missing a Phase 1 camp does not automatically transfer the entitlement to Phase 2, so checking the updated list is essential.

Smartphones under this scheme are not distributed through shops or online channels. They are handed out exclusively at specially organised IGSY distribution camps, which are set up at district and block levels across Rajasthan.

Families who are not registered under Chiranjeevi but believe they qualify for the scheme should first get their Chiranjeevi registration done through the state portal at chiranjeevi.rajasthan.gov.in and then check for IGSY eligibility.

extra_sections.text: When a woman in a Chiranjeevi family gets a smartphone with three years of data, she gains access to government portals, banking, education, and health services entirely on her own terms. The Rs 6,800 grant is not just a phone; it is an entry point to everything digital Rajasthan has to offer.

extra_sections.heading: Other Things to Know
content: Camp schedules are announced in advance through official channels including the igsy.rajasthan.gov.in portal, local gram panchayat notice boards, and the state government's social media handles. Beneficiaries should track the camp schedule for their block or district.

At the camp, beneficiaries must bring their original Jan Aadhaar card and Aadhaar card for verification. A biometric check or document check is conducted before the smartphone is handed over and the e-wallet amount is credited.

The e-wallet amount of Rs 6,800 is credited to the beneficiary's Jan Aadhaar-linked account at the time of smartphone distribution at the camp. The money is specifically earmarked for the smartphone and SIM purchase and is not transferable as cash.
The scheme's official website is igsy.rajasthan.gov.in. This portal hosts the beneficiary list, camp information, and the official scheme guidelines for the Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana.

District authorities are responsible for announcing camp dates in their respective areas. Beneficiaries are advised to register their mobile number with the Jan Aadhaar system so they receive SMS alerts about upcoming camp schedules in their block or district.

faqs.question: What is Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana Rajasthan?
faqs.answer: Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana is a Rajasthan government scheme that provides free smartphones with a SIM card and three years of free internet data to eligible women and girl students. The government transfers Rs 6,800 to the beneficiary's e-wallet, covering the smartphone (Rs 6,175) and SIM plus data plan (Rs 625).

faqs.question: Is Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana still active in 2025?
faqs.answer:
Phase 1 distributed about 40 lakh smartphones before the December 2023 state election. After the change of government, Phase 2 stalled.

Only about 24.5 lakh of roughly 1.33 crore targeted women had received phones, and the scheme has been under review. Treat distribution as paused and check the official portal for any restart.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana?
faqs.answer: Eligible categories include widow and destitute women on state pension, girl students in Class 9-12 of government schools, girls in government colleges, polytechnic institutes, and ITIs, women who completed 100 days under MNREGA, and women who completed 50 days under IGSRGS. All must be from Chiranjeevi-registered families.

faqs.question: What is the official website for Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana?
faqs.answer: The official portal is igsy.rajasthan.gov.in. Beneficiary list and eligibility status can also be checked on jansoochna.rajasthan.gov.in using the Jan Aadhaar number.

faqs.question: How do I get a smartphone under Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana?
faqs.answer:
First check your eligibility on jansoochna.rajasthan.gov.in using your Jan Aadhaar number. Then find the camp date and location for your area through igsy.rajasthan.gov.in or by calling helpline 181.

Attend the camp with your Jan Aadhaar card and Aadhaar card to receive the smartphone.

faqs.question: What is the helpline for Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana?
faqs.answer: The toll-free helpline for Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana Rajasthan is 181. You can call this number for camp schedules, eligibility queries, complaints, or any issue related to the scheme.

faqs.question: What documents are needed at the IGSY distribution camp?
faqs.answer: You need to bring your original Jan Aadhaar card and your Aadhaar card to the distribution camp. Verification is done through the Jan Aadhaar system, so the card must be the one linked to your household registration.

faqs.question: What is the Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana official website?
faqs.answer: The official website is igsy.rajasthan.gov.in. This portal has the scheme details, camp schedule, and beneficiary list for the Indira Gandhi Free Smartphone Scheme in Rajasthan.

faqs.question: How much money is given under Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana?
faqs.answer:
The government credits Rs 6,800 to the beneficiary's e-wallet. Of this, Rs 6,175 is for the smartphone and Rs 625 covers the SIM card and three years of free internet data.

The amount is directly used for the smartphone purchase at the distribution camp.

faqs.question: Can a woman check her name in the Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana list?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Visit jansoochna.rajasthan.gov.in and look for the Indira Gandhi Smartphone Yojana section.

Enter your Jan Aadhaar number to check whether you appear in the beneficiary list. You can also call helpline 181 for assistance.
